findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 58 mm is observed in the tail of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the splenic vein, suggesting invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastases are observed in two nodes at station 2. Two hypodense masses are observed in the right lobe of the liver, raising suspicion of liver metastases.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU0 (no invasion of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A0 (no invasion of the arterial branches)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (contact of more than 180° with the splenic vein, suggesting invasion)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the local invasion factors, the T classification is T3, as there is serosal invasion (S1) and contact of more than 180° with the splenic vein (OO1).

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the tail are:
- Station 2 (left gastric artery and common hepatic artery lymph nodes)
- Station 3 (cystic duct and common bile duct lymph nodes)
- Station 4 (hilar lymph nodes)
- Station 5 (peripancreatic lymph nodes)

The patient's metastatic lymph node stations are:
- Station 2

Since Station 2 is a regional lymph node, we count the metastatic lymph nodes within this station:
- 2 nodes at Station 2

N classification: N1a (1-4 regional lymph nodes involved)

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There are two hypodense masses in the right lobe of the liver, raising suspicion of liver metastases. This indicates the presence of distant metastases.

M classification: M1 (distant metastasis)

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor is unresectable due to distant metastasis.

Resectability classification: Unresectable (UR)

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T (T3), N (N1a), and M (M1) categories, the overall stage is Stage IV.
